item.title: Chrome Builds a Mirror Universe for Agents: Testing Browser Proxies Without Touching the Real Network | CN-SEC
item.description: This article reveals the 'Mirror Dimension' synthetic network constructed by the Chrome Security Team. By leveraging dynamic certificate forgery and multi-agent collaboration generation, it successfully addresses the evaluation challenges of browser agents in real networks, such as non-reproducibility, uncontrollability, and exposure of testing intentions. This solution not only enables high-fidelity automated red team exercises but also critically overcomes the model's 'evaluation awareness' trap, setting a new engineering benchmark for the secure iteration of AI agents.

item.title: Ghostscript Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2026-125396): Bypassing -dSAFER Sandbox via Use-After-Free Affects Roundcube and WordPress
item.description: The core highlight of this article is the revelation of a remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-125396) in Ghostscript that can be triggered through ordinary image uploads. It successfully bypasses the -dSAFER sandbox by exploiting a use-after-free defect in the Type 1 font loader. The article not only provides complete proof-of-concept code but also profoundly points out that this vulnerability has evolved into a supply-chain-level threat affecting a wide ecosystem including WordPress, CUPS, and Google services, forcing security teams to immediately investigate unpatched components in containers and bundles...

item.title: VirtualBox Process Hardening on Windows 2026 Edition: What's a Single Bit Between Friends?
item.description: Back in 2017 I did some research into Oracle VirtualBox on Windows. Specifically I focussed on their mechanism to protect their VM processes from the user on the host. The protection was to gate who could open the kernel driver, which might allow for privilege escalation due to the way it was designed. At the time I found 3 ways of bypassing the protection, with an additional issue in COM’s runtime I reported in 2020. These issues were all written up in this post.

item.title: Windows DLL Load Anomaly Detection (Part 1)
item.description: Windows DLL Load Anomaly Detection (Part 1): Was the check really performed after the DLL was queued? The startup enumeration sent plugins into the verification queue. When worker threads retrieved them, they skipped them directly because 'this path has already been registered.' Looking down AntiHijackDlls.cpp, the problem lies in the usage of the same set in two places. Enumeration uses it to record seen paths, while worker threads use it to decide whether further checks are needed.

item.title: WHMCS SQL Injection Could Expose Customer Data and Admin Password Hashes without Login
item.description: A flaw in WHMCS 's shopping cart, the billing and automation platform many web hosting companies use to run their businesses, could allow anyone on the internet to retrieve customer records and administrator password hashes from an installation's database. No login is needed. The company disclosed the SQL injection yesterday along with two other flaws that need a logged-in client, and released fixed versions. It has not reported attacks using any of the three. Because no login is needed, the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-82981 (CVSS score: 8.7), is within reach of anyone who can load the shopping cart of a vulnerable installation over the internet. The records an attacker could pull include clients' personal and support information as well as admin accounts with their hashed passwords, according to the company's advisory. item.title: OpenAI and Cisco Unveil AI-Assisted Linux Security Tool to Block Exploits Before Patching
item.description: OpenAI and Cisco have teamed up to launch Shirudo (meaning "shield" in Japanese), an open-source Linux runtime that allows artificial intelligence (AI) agents to defend systems without downtime. "It lets agents write dynamic eBPF controls to shield systems from exploits, giving defenders more time to test and roll out patches," OpenAI said in a post on X. The AI upstart called the initiative a "first step" toward "self-defending infrastructure" that can adapt itself to new threats while the services continue to run and enable defenders to test and deploy fixes without any disruption. The development comes as AI is accelerating vulnerability discovery, finding critical bugs in foundational software used to power internet-connected software. item.title: Webworm Suspected of Modifying SoftEther VPN to Evade Detection and Hide Remote Access
item.description: The China-aligned threat actor known as Webworm is suspected to be using a custom version of the open-source SoftEther VPN Bridge tool in an attempt to remove recognizable detection fingerprints, while disguising it as network-monitoring software to establish covert remote access to compromised networks. The modified variant "implements various tricks to hide itself from security tools," Rapid7 said in an analysis, attributing it to the adversarial collective with moderate confidence. First publicly detailed by Broadcom-owned Symantec in September 2022, Webworm is the name assigned to a China-aligned nation-state group that has targeted government entities, IT services, and electric power companies across Russia, Georgia, Mongolia, and several other Asian nations. One of the tools used by the threat actor is a legitimate software called SoftEther VPN , with the bridge acting as a pathway connecting the compromised network and the attacker-controlled infrastructure...

item.description: A stolen key. A trusted message. A routine update. None of these looks like the start of a major security problem. That's partly why they work. item.description: A critical security flaw has been disclosed in the popular binary-parser library that could allow an attacker who controls parser definitions to execute arbitrary code. item.title: N-able Discloses Critical Mail Assure Vulnerability Found During Breach Investigation
item.description: N-able yesterday disclosed a critical flaw it found while investigating the breach of its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud, an email filtering service it runs for managed service providers. The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-134624 , is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) flaw. It allowed a user with high-level API access to open connections to internal systems of the user's choosing on the platform's servers. The company fixed the flaw and restored access to the dashboard and APIs late on Saturday, closing an outage that began last Monday. Email delivery and spam filtering kept working throughout, according to the company. It has not said whether the flaw was the attackers' way in. The bug sat in a connection check that Mail Assure runs for LDAP synchronization when a relay is configured. item.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ASP.NET Anti-CSRF Library Flaw Allowing Unauthenticated RCE
item.description: Cybersecurity researchers have urged users to discontinue using a legacy ASP.NET anti-CSRF library named Idunno.AntiCsrf ("Idunno.AntiCsrf.dll") following the discovery of a critical vulnerability that has been exploited in the wild. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-131914 , carries a CVSS score of 9.3 out of 10.0. The issue affects versions 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta, and relates to an insecure deserialization vulnerability in the Idunno.AntiCsrf.AntiCsrfModule HTTP module. Idunno.AntiCsrf is a third-party ASP.NET IHttpModule designed to provide double-submit cookie Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) protection for ASP.NET WebForms applications. The open-source project is currently defunct and has not been updated since December 2008. At its core, the problem stems from the fact that the module deserializes untrusted CSRF form token data using an unkeyed .NET System.Web.UI.ObjectStateFormatter instance without cryptographic MAC or signature verification when handlin...

The company identified and fixed the flaw on Friday and blocked the access the attacker used, so devices can no longer be infected through this route. The cloud-side fix does not remove malware from devices that were already infected, so owners still need to check their hardware and install the security firmware listed today. A KVM is a small device used to control a computer remotely as if sitting in front of it. The company is still investigating whether computers attached to infected KVMs were affected.
